Tweaks.RecipeListCompletionMarks.Name: Recipe List completion marks
Tweaks.RecipeListCompletionMarks.Descrip: Shows the Crafting Log check mark next to every recipe in the "Recipes List" window that you have already crafted, so you can tell at a glance what is still left to make. By default an item counts only for the class of its section; an option counts it if any class crafted it.
Tweaks.RecipeListCompletionMarks.Command: Opens or closes the help of Recipe List completion marks.
Tweaks.RecipeListCompletionMarks.Help.Te:
What it does
In the "Recipes List" window (the list of recipes of an item or a crafting class) every recipe you have already crafted gets the same check mark the Crafting Log shows. Recipes you have not crafted stay without it.

Where to look
Open "Recipes List" from the Crafting Log or from the recipe window. The marks appear on the left of each row, over the corner of the item icon.

Option
In the Settings of this tweak, "Count recipes of any class": if an item can be crafted by several classes, it is marked when you crafted it with any of them, not only with the class of its section.

Commands
/grm or /gmarks opens or closes this help.
Tweaks.RecipeListCompletionMarks.AnyClas: If an item can be crafted by several classes, mark it when you crafted it with any of them, not only with the class of its section.

It is an estimate: memory owned by the game itself is not counted.

Tweaks.CraftingMaterials.Name: Crafting Materials Inventory
Tweaks.CraftingMaterials.Description: Shows all craftable recipes cross-referenced with everything you own: your inventories, saddlebag, retainers and FC chest. For every recipe you see its ingredients, how many you already have and where they are, so you know what is missing before you start crafting. It can also outline the items you need in the FC chest window.
Tweaks.CraftingMaterials.Command.Help: Opens or closes the Crafting Materials Inventory window.
Tweaks.CraftingMaterials.Language.Help: Language for item and recipe names shown in this window. Independent of the GoblinTweaks language; defaults to it.
Tweaks.CraftingMaterials.IncludeRetainer: Retainer data is cached after visiting the retainer bell. May be incomplete if retainers have not been visited this session.
Tweaks.CraftingMaterials.Highlight: Highlight items in bags, retainers, saddlebag and FC Chest
Tweaks.CraftingMaterials.Highlight.Help: While your inventory, a retainer's inventory, the chocobo saddlebag or the FC chest is open, outlines the slots holding the ingredients of the selected recipe, and pulses the tabs that have some. The FC chest also needs "Include FC Chest". For it to work properly, sorting your inventories (bags, retainers, saddlebag) is recommended.
Reads from the FC chest if it was opened this session and you have withdrawal permissions.

Tweaks.RetainerVentureTimer.Name: Retainer Venture Timer
Tweaks.RetainerVentureTimer.Description: Adds an entry to the Server Info Bar with a countdown to the next retainer returning from a venture, and shows "Ready!" when one is done. Hover over it to see every retainer on a venture with its own countdown. The entry stays hidden while no retainer is on a venture.
Tweaks.RetainerVentureTimer.Command.Help: Opens or closes the help of Retainer Venture Timer.
Tweaks.RetainerVentureTimer.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.RetainerVentureTimer.Help.Text:
What it does
Shows a countdown to the next retainer returning from a venture, so you do not have to open the retainer list to know when to go back.

Where to look
In the Server Info Bar, the strip of entries on the top of the screen (next to the clock and the FPS). The entry is called "Venture Timer" and shows ⚗ and the time left, for example ⚗ 1h 25m. When a venture is done it says "Ready!".

Details
Hover over the entry to see every retainer on a venture and how long each one has left. The entry stays hidden while no retainer is on a venture.

Right after you log in it asks the server for your retainers, as the game's Timers window does, so the countdown shows up without going to a summoning bell.

If you do not see it
Open the Dalamud settings (/xlsettings) and, in the Server Info Bar tab, make sure "Venture Timer" is ticked.

Commands
/grvt or /gretimer opens or closes this help.
Tweaks.SquadronTimer.Name: Squadron Mission & Training Timer
Tweaks.SquadronTimer.Description: Adds an entry to the Server Info Bar with a countdown to the next squadron mission or training session to complete, and shows "Ready!" when one is done. Hover over it to see both timers. The entry stays hidden while there is no mission or training in progress.
Tweaks.SquadronTimer.Command.Help: Opens or closes the help of Squadron Mission & Training Timer.
Tweaks.SquadronTimer.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.SquadronTimer.Help.Text:
What it does
Shows a countdown to the next squadron mission or training session to complete, so you do not have to visit the barracks to check.

Where to look
In the Server Info Bar, the strip of entries on the top of the screen (next to the clock and the FPS). The entry is called "Squadron Timer" and shows ⚔ and the time left of whichever finishes first, for example ⚔ 45m 10s. When one is done it says "Ready!".

Details
Hover over the entry to see the mission and the training with their own timers. The entry stays hidden while there is no mission or training in progress.

If you do not see it
Open the Dalamud settings (/xlsettings) and, in the Server Info Bar tab, make sure "Squadron Timer" is ticked.

Commands
/gst or /gsquadron opens or closes this help.
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Name: Weapon pose per job
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Description: Remembers the pose (/cpose) you choose with your weapon drawn separately for every job, and puts it back when you switch to that job and draw your weapon. Open its window to see every job with its saved pose.
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Command.Help: Opens or closes the Weapon pose per job window.
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Open.Help: Opens the list of jobs and their saved poses.
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Title: Weapon Poses
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Help.Text:
The game keeps a single weapon-drawn pose for all jobs. This tweak remembers one for each job.

To save a pose: draw your weapon and use /cpose until you like it. It is saved for your current job automatically.

When you switch to a job with a saved pose, it is put back as soon as you draw your weapon outside of combat.

"Default" means no pose has been saved for that job yet.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Name: GoblinSniper
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Description: Watches the Market Board for listings priced far below what the item normally sells for (like a mount listed at 100,000 gil instead of 1,000,000) and lists them with their discount, resale chance and the age of the data. Prices come from Universalis. You choose which kinds of items to watch; scans run by themselves and the number of deals found shows in the Server Info Bar.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Command.Help: Opens or closes the GoblinSniper window.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Language.Help: Language of the item names in the window and in the search below. Independent of the GoblinTweaks language; defaults to it.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Notify: Show in the Server Info Bar
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Notify.Help: Adds an entry with the number of deals found. Click it to open the window.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.WholeDataCenter.Help: Looks at every world of your data center, not only your home world. You have to visit the world to buy.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Discount.Help: A listing must be at least this far below the normal price, and below the next seller.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.MinPrice.Help: Items that normally sell for less than this are ignored.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.MaxAge.Help: Ignores listings whose price was uploaded longer ago than this. Lower means fewer deals, but more reliable ones.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.MaxDays.Help: Ignores items nobody has bought in more than this many days: they would just sit on the market.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Types.Help: Every marketable item of the chosen types is watched. The number is how many items each type adds. The big types (weapons, armor, furnishings) make each scan take a few minutes.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Items.Help: Watch individual items of any type. Search by name and click a result to add it.

Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.About.Title: What it does
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.About.Text:
GoblinSniper looks for listings priced far below what the item normally sells for. Most of the time the seller made a typo: a mount listed at 100,000 gil instead of 1,000,000.

A listing counts as a deal only if all of this is true:

- It is below the average price by at least the discount you chose.
- It is also that far below the next seller. If everyone lists low, the price simply dropped.
- The item normally sells for more than your minimum price.
- The data is not older than your maximum data age.
- Someone bought the item recently (within 60 days by default).

With a low discount (30%) you will mostly see price differences between worlds. Raise it to keep only real mistakes.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Columns.Title: Columns
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Columns.Text:
Item: icon, name and type. Hover a row to see the game's tooltip. Click a row to copy the item name, then paste it in the search of a market board.

iLvl: the item level.

Avg. price: the average sale price over the last few days in the area being scanned. If the item rarely sells, the price of its last sale is used.

Listed price: the cheapest listing right now, in green. Below it, "Next" is the cheapest listing from a different seller.

Discount: how far the listed price is below the average price.

World: where the listing is. To buy it, you have to travel to that world.

Updated: how long ago that price was uploaded.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Resale.Title: Resale chance
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Resale.Text:
The Resale column estimates how likely you are to sell the item again on your home world within 7 days.

It comes from "sales per day", a figure Universalis calculates from the last few days of sales and shows under the percentage. At 0.1 sales per day (one every 10 days) the chance is about 50%; at 0.5 per day it is about 97%.

Green is 75% or more, yellow is 40% or more, red is less.

If your world has no recent sales, an even share of the whole data center's sales is used instead.

It is only an estimate: it assumes you list at a price people will pay, and it does not know how many other sellers you compete with.

Items nobody has bought for too long are left out of the list: 60 days by default, see "Maximum days without a sale" in the settings. Universalis does not say how long a listing has been up, so this is judged by the last sale of the item.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Sorting.Title: Sorting and filters
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Sorting.Text:
"Sort by" only changes the order of the list: biggest discount (in %), biggest saving (in gil), lowest price, highest avg. price, item level, name, item type, world, or most recently updated.

The two lists next to it are filters, and they do hide rows:

- World: only the deals of one world. It lists the worlds that have a deal right now.
- Data age: only the deals whose price was uploaded less than 1, 3, 6 or 12 hours ago.

The search box filters by item name or world name.

The small X next to the search box clears it. The round arrow next to the filters resets them to all worlds and any data age.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Data.Title: Prices and data age
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Data.Text:
The game cannot show you the market board of another world, so prices come from Universalis, a public site that players feed when they open an item on a market board.

That is why data has an age. "Updated: 15h" means nobody has looked at that item on that world for 15 hours, so the listing may already be sold.

The plugin cannot make the data newer, but you can: travel to that world and open the item on the market board, and it is uploaded right away.

Popular items are refreshed all the time. Rare ones can go many hours without an update.

To see only recent data, lower "Maximum data age" in the settings. You will get fewer deals, but more reliable ones.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Scanning.Title: Scans and alerts
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Scanning.Text:
A scan runs shortly after you log in, every few minutes (see the settings), when you change a setting, and when you press the scan button (the arrows, top right). The gear next to it opens the settings.

Deals appear as they are found, without waiting for the scan to end. A deal from the previous scan stays listed until its item is checked again.

The scan button is locked until the scan ends, so a scan cannot be started twice. The bottom bar shows the progress.

The number in the Server Info Bar is how many deals are on the list right now. Click it to open this window, or hover to see the best ones.

If the bottom bar says Universalis is overloaded or did not answer, nothing is wrong on your side. What was found is kept, and the scan is retried in a couple of minutes.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Items.Title: Which items are watched
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Items.Text:
Only what you choose in the settings is scanned, not the whole game. "Items watched" in the bottom bar is that total.

Item types: mounts, minions, orchestrion rolls, Triple Triad cards, bardings, fashion accessories, hairstyles and emotes, dyes, materia, workshop parts, other collectibles, weapons, armor and furnishings. Each shows how many items it adds.

Weapons, armor and furnishings have thousands of items, so a scan that includes them takes a few minutes.

Specific items: search for any item by name in the settings and click it to watch it, whatever its type.

Only items that can be sold on the market board are included. The language of the item names is chosen in the settings.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Name: Goblin Battle Text
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Description: Shows the damage and healing you deal and take around the center of the screen, where your character stands, instead of over the target. It also announces buffs, debuffs and cooldowns, and tells apart criticals, misses, blocks, immunities and damage over time. Events, areas, colors, fonts and the order of each message are all configurable.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Open.Help: Opens the settings window. Sample text scrolls while it is open.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Title: Goblin Battle Text
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Positionals:
Some actions hit harder from the rear or the flank of the target (Gekko, Kasha, Gibbet, Gallows, Fang and Claw...). This tweak tells you whether you hit that positional. Which actions have one, and on which side, is read from the game's own description of each action, so there is no list to keep up to date.

The game never says whether you hit it, so it is worked out from two things:
- The bonus. Each hit reports how much of its potency is bonus (combo plus positional). The potencies in the action's description, at your level (synced or not), tell what the bonus is with the positional and without it.
- Where you stood. The rear is the quarter of the circle behind the enemy, 45° to each side of its back. The flanks are the two quarters at its sides.

The verdict:
- No bonus at all: missed.
- Action with no combo (Gibbet, Trick Attack...): any bonus is the positional, so hit.
- The bonus of a hit: hit.
- The bonus of a miss, or an unexpected one (an effect is raising the potency): where you stood decides.

True North, enemies with no sides and effects that remove positionals count as hit, as in the game. Actions that deal no damage say nothing.

Turn it on, choose its area, or show it in the damage message in the Events tab. Its look is in the Highlights tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.OverTime.Te:
The game sends damage over time (DoT) and healing over time (HoT) ticks with no action attached: one number per target every 3 seconds.

Name and icon: those of the effect that ticks, like 132 Higanbana or +78 Regen. If several effects tick, all are named, and so are effects on the ground, like Doton. If none is found, the tick just says (DoT) or (HoT).

Whose tick it is:
- Sometimes the game says who applied it (healing over time, ground effects). Then you only see yours and your pet's, and the number is exact.
- Usually it does not (most damage over time). The game sends one sum of everyone's damage on that enemy. If none of it is yours, nothing is shown. If only yours is there, the number is exact. If others are on the enemy too, your share is an estimate, split by effect.

Where it appears:
- Healing over time on you counts as healing received, whoever gave it.
- On anyone else (your pet included) it counts as healing given, and only shows if you or your pet gave it.
- Damage over time on you counts as damage taken.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Rules.Title: What counts as yours
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Rules.Text:
Debuffs on enemies: only yours. You see + name when it starts and - name when it ends. The same debuff from another player of your job is told apart. Nothing is shown when the enemy dies.

Pets: with Include my pet and chocobo (General tab), whatever your pet or chocobo deals, heals or applies to others counts as yours, including when it heals itself.

Counterattacks: when an effect like Vengeance or Damnation hits back, the message shows the name and icon of that action instead of a plain Attack.

Auto-attacks: when they are not yours, they say who made them, like Attack Kweh, or the name of the enemy hitting you. Actions of your pet or chocobo also end with its name.

Merged hits: with the Merge options (General tab), an action that hits several targets shows one total and the number of hits. Hits merge only with hits of the same kind: normal with normal, direct with direct, critical with critical and critical direct with critical direct.

Effects that fail: if an enemy is immune to the effect of your action, or fully resists it, the action says so after its name, like Leg Sweep Immune, in the miss color. It appears where actions with no damage appear.

Actions with no damage: an action of your job that deals no damage and heals nothing shows its icon and name, like a dash or a stun such as Leg Sweep. If it only puts an effect on you, that effect is announced instead.

Effects like Bloodbath: what an attack heals you for counts as healing received.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.PositionalInline: Shows whether you hit the positional in the damage message, after the action name, instead of in a separate alert. The area and movement set for the positional alert then do not apply: it appears where the damage does.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Positional: Shows whether you hit the positional of an action that hits harder from the rear or the flank. Choose its area and movement here, or show it in the damage message with the option below. Its look is in the Highlights tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Positi: Gives the alert for a positional you hit its own look. Off: it uses its area's font and size, in green.
Gives the alert for a positional you missed its own look. Off: it uses its area's font and size, in red.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Gradie: Blends the text from the alert color to a second color.
Whether the gradient goes from left to right or from top to bottom.
The color the gradient ends on.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeHeals.Help: An action that heals several targets at once shows one total with the number of heals. Off: one message per target.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShowHealTargets: Show who my healing and shields are for
Heals and shields you give end with the name of who gets them, in brackets. Merged ones have several targets and name none: turn off Merge healing on several targets to see each name.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.ActionUsed: An action of your job that deals no damage, heals nothing and applies no effect, like a dash. The game shows no text for these.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.Star: Left: messages start at the area position and grow to the right.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.Midd: Center: messages are centered on the area position.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.End: Right: messages end at the area position and grow to the left.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Animat: Kind of animation. Choosing one lists its animations on the right and plays the first.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Cooldowns.Hint: Click to turn on or off. Lit: announced. Hover for the name.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Colors.Help: One color per kind of text. Click a color to open the color picker.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Order.None: No event is sent to this area. Choose where each event goes in the Events tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Preview.Hint: Sample text is on. Drag each area's box to move it. Press ? for help.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeHits.Help: An attack that hits several targets at once shows a single total with the number of hits.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeMisses.Help: Misses, dodges and invulnerable hits of one action show as one message with the number of times, like Miss x3. Off: one message each.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeDefended.He: Blocked, parried and resisted hits of one action merge, each kind with its own kind. Off: they show one by one.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeNoEffect.He: An effect that fails on several targets of one action shows once with the number of times, like Leg Sweep Immune x3. Off: one message each.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeTicks: Merge damage and healing over time
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeTicks.Help: The ticks of one effect on several targets, like your Higanbana on three enemies, show as one message with the number of ticks, like 132 Higanbana x3. Off: one message per tick.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeWindow.Help: How long, in tenths of a second, a message stays open to take in more hits of the same action. Raise it if one attack on several targets still shows as several messages. Normal hits merge with normal ones and critical hits with critical ones, never with each other.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeAmount.Help: The number a merged message shows: the total of all its hits (474 Fire II x3), or the average of them, rounded to a whole number (158 Fire II x3).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShieldMode.Help: What your player window says while you have a shield (Haima, Eukrasian Prognosis...). Added: the HP number shows HP plus shield in the blue of the shield (18,325 HP and a 2,000 shield show 20,325). Below: the shield is written in blue under the HP number, in the same font and aligned to its right. The game only tells the shield as a percentage of your maximum HP, so the amount can be off by some dozens.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.OutlineEnabled.H: Draws an outline around the letters of every message. Its color is in the Colors section below.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.OutlineThickness: Width of the outline, in pixels. Wider outlines draw each message more times, which costs a little more.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.HpOutlineEnabled: Draws an outline around the HP and MP numbers and their labels in your player window, and around the shield written under the HP. The game's outline is one pixel wide; the color is chosen on the right.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.IncludePets.Help: What your pet or chocobo deals is shown as outgoing.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.IncludeNpcs.Help: What the NPCs that fight beside you in a duty (Trust, Duty Support, story companions) deal is shown as outgoing, as if it were yours. Off by default: they are not your pet.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.IncludeNpcHealin: Also show the healing of those NPCs (and their healing over time) as yours. Needs the option above. Off by default: it is theirs, not yours.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShowDefended.Hel: Damage that was blocked, parried or resisted says so after the number, like -270 (parried). Off: only the number shows.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Mitigation.Help: Adds how much of the damage you take was removed by your damage reduction. Percent only: -270 (-30%). With the word: -270 (-30% mitigated). It is worked out from the effects active at that moment, using the percentages in the descriptions of the actions that give them.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Font.Help: Font of every message. Size is set per area, in the Areas tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Enabled.Hel: Off: these events use the game's own floating text.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.OffsetX.Hel: Pixels to the right (positive) or left (negative) of the center of the screen.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.OffsetY.Hel: Pixels below (positive) or above (negative) the center of the screen.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.Help: Which point of each message sits on the area position. 0: the message starts there and grows to the right. 50: centered. 100: it ends there and grows to the left.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Height.Help: Pixels a message travels before it disappears.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.FontSize.He: Text size for this area. Highlighted messages (special hits, cooldown alerts) have their own size, set in the Highlights and Cooldowns tabs.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Duration.He: Seconds a message stays on screen.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.MinAmount.H: Damage and healing below this amount is hidden, both here and in the game's own text. 0 shows everything.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Style.Help: Path of this area's messages: straight, curved to one side, or Static (they stay in place, fade, and pile up as more arrive).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Order: Order of each message in this area
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Order.Help: Left-to-right order of the parts of a message in this area. Arrows move a part; the eye hides or shows it. Only parts used by events sent to this area are listed. Each area has its own order.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Part.Name: Action name
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.LimitBreak: An alert each time a bar of the Limit Break gauge of your party fills, like Limit Break Lv 2 ready!
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShowFading.Help: Buffs and debuffs are announced when they end (- name) as well as when they start (+ name).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Area.Help: Where this event appears: Outgoing (right of your character), Incoming (left) or Center (below).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DamageDeal: Damage you, your pet or your damage over time deal, with misses.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DamageTake: Damage you receive, with what you dodge.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.ShieldDeal: The shield you put on others (Succor, Haima...). The game gives no text for it: the amount is worked out from how much it raised their shield, so it can be off by some dozens.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.ShieldTake: The shield you get, from yourself or from others. Worked out from how much it raised your shield, so it can be off by some dozens.
Healing you receive, from yourself or from others.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Mp.Help: MP you recover from actions and effects.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.BuffOnMe.H: A beneficial effect starts or ends on you, whoever gave it.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.BuffOnOthe: A beneficial effect you put on someone else starts.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DebuffOnMe: A harmful effect starts or ends on you.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DebuffOnEn: A harmful effect of yours starts or ends on an enemy.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Cooldown.H: Announces when one of the actions ticked below is ready to use again.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Cooldowns.Help: Click an action to turn its alert on or off. Lit: announced. Dimmed: not. The list is for the job you had when this window opened.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Cooldowns.None: No actions with a cooldown found. Log in on a combat job and reopen this window.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Command.Help: Opens or closes the Goblin Battle Text settings.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Motion.Hel: How this event moves: up, down or Static (stays in place and fades). If an area's path is Static, all its events stay still.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.CooldownOrder.He: Left to right order of the parts of a cooldown alert. The eye hides or shows a part.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Overview.Te:
Goblin Battle Text replaces the numbers that float over the target with text around the center of the screen, where your character stands, so you never lose sight of it. The game's own numbers for those events are hidden, so nothing shows twice.

There are three areas:
- Outgoing, right of your character: what you do.
- Incoming, left: what happens to you.
- Center, below: effects that start or end, and cooldowns.

Each kind of event can go to any area, or be turned off.

Open this window with /gbt or from the tweak card in GoblinTweaks. While it is open, sample text scrolls so you can see each change at once, and each area has a named box you can drag to move it. Settings save automatically and are per character: a character seen for the first time starts with a copy of your current settings. The name under this window's title says whose settings you are editing.

Hold the button at the bottom right to reset the tab you are looking at to its defaults.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.General.Tex:
Merge damage / healing on several targets: an area attack or heal shows one total with the number of hits. Each has its own switch.

Show who my healing is for: heals you give end with the name of who they heal, unless they are merged.

Damage and healing over time: the game sends one tick per target with everyone's damage added up. When others also have effects on that target, yours is shown as an estimate.

Shorten large numbers: 12.3K instead of 12,345.

Include my pet and chocobo: their damage counts as yours.

Show blocked, parried and resisted: whether such hits say so after the number.

Mitigated: adds how much of the damage you take was removed, as a percent only, like -270 (-30%), or with the word, like -270 (-30% mitigated). It counts effects on you that reduce damage (Rampart, Damnation, Kerachole...) and effects on the attacker that lower its damage (Reprisal, Feint, Addle...), each with the percent in its action's description. Several multiply, as in the game. Blocks, parries, barriers and anything without a percent in its description are not counted.

Font: the font of every message. Size is set per area, in the Areas tab.

Colors: one per kind of text: damage dealt, damage taken, healing, misses and dodges, MP gained, actions with no damage, and buffs and debuffs (one color when they start, another when they end). Click a color to open the picker: Confirm applies it, Default restores the original, Cancel leaves it as it was.

The colors of critical and direct hits are in the Highlights tab; those of the cooldown alert are in the Cooldowns tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Areas.Title: Areas tab
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Areas.Text:
Choose the area at the top: Outgoing, Incoming or Center. All three have the same settings. The Restore button only affects the one you are looking at, and the cog next to the switch copies this area's look to another.

Show this area: off, its events go back to the game's own text.

Position X and Y: where the area is, in pixels from the center of the screen (negative is left or up). Drag the area's box on screen, move the slider, or type the exact number with + and -.

Alignment: 0, messages start at the area position and grow to the right. 50, centered. 100, they end there and grow to the left. The three buttons set those values.

Scroll distance, Font size and Duration (in seconds).

Minimum amount: smaller damage and healing is not shown.

Messages at once: how many show at the same time, 1 to 15. When another arrives, the oldest disappears.

Path: straight, curved to one side, or Static (messages stay in place and fade).

Order of each message: arrows move a part earlier or later; the eye hides or shows it. Only parts used by events sent to this area are listed.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Events.Text:
One row per kind of event, with three settings:

- The checkbox turns the event on or off. Off, the game shows it as usual.
- Area: Outgoing, Incoming or Center.
- Movement: up, down or Static.

Events: Damage dealt and Damage taken (with misses and dodges), Healing on allies, Healing received (including what effects like Bloodbath heal you for), MP gained, Buff on me, Debuff on me, Buff I give, Debuff on enemy, and Action with no damage (dashes and other actions the game shows no text for).

Announce effects that end: buffs and debuffs show + name when they start and - name when they wear off.

Messages never cross. When an area has events going up and events going down, each direction gets half of the area and starts from its middle. Static events pile up just outside the scrolling path. If the halves feel short, raise the area's scroll distance.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Cooldowns.T:
Cooldown alerts tell you when an action is ready again, like "Fast Blade ready now!". They are off until you tick the checkbox at the top. Next to it you choose the area and how the alert moves.

Own look for the alert: font, size, animation, intensity and the color of the "ready now!" text. Off, the alert uses its area's font and size, in white. The action name always has its own color.

Order of the cooldown alert: its three parts (icon, action name, "ready now!" text). Arrows move a part; the eye hides it.

Actions of your current job: click one to turn its alert on or off (lit: announced). Hover to see its name, or type part of it in the search box.

Which actions are listed: those of your job, at your level, with their own cooldown of 5 seconds or more (not the global one). Actions that share a cooldown, like an action and its upgrade, count once. The alert comes when the cooldown ends; with charges, when all of them are back. The list is for the job you had when the window opened: after changing job, close and reopen it.

Procs are not listed. An effect that makes an action available shows as Buff on me.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Defaults.Help: Hold down to reset every setting of the current tab to its default. In the Areas tab, only the current area is reset. Other tabs are not touched.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Critic: Gives critical hits (marked with !) their own look. Off: they look like any other hit in their area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Direct: Gives direct hits their own look. Off: they look like any other hit in their area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Critic: Gives critical direct hits (marked with !!) their own look. Off: they look like any other hit in their area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Cooldo: Gives cooldown alerts their own look. Off: they use their area's font and size, with white text.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Font.H: Font of this kind of message, in place of the general one.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Animat: What the message does when it appears: choose the kind first, then the animation. There are 35; the sample text plays the one you pick, so try a few.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.FontSi: Size of this kind of message, in place of that of its area.
Choose at the top what to set: critical hits (!), direct hits, critical direct hits (!!), and the alerts for a positional you hit or missed. Each has its own look. The look of the cooldown alert is in the Cooldowns tab.

Positional alerts: when you use an action that hits harder from the rear or the flank (Gekko, Kasha, Gibbet...), an alert says whether you hit it from there. True North counts as a hit. Turn them on or off, and choose their area, in the Events tab.

- Checkbox: off, the message looks like any other in its area.
- Colors: one for damage you deal and one for damage you take. Critical hits have a third for healing, the only other thing that can be critical.
- Gradient (positional alerts): blends the text from its color to a second one, left to right or top to bottom.
- Font and Font size, instead of the area's.
- Animation, played when the message appears: pick its kind in the first list and the animation in the second.
- Intensity: strength of the animation, 0 to 300; 100 is normal.

Gentle: Pop, Shake, Pulse, Flash.
Impacts: Slam, Quake, Earthquake, Stomp, Crush, Shockwave, Meteor, Fury.
Size: Bounce, Zoom, Stretch, Explode, Heartbeat.
Rotation: Swing, Rattle, Spin, Tornado.
Movement: Drop, Launch, Dash, Recoil.
Light: Blaze, Thunder, Ignite, Ember, Frost, Venom, Blood, Radiance, Shadow, Strobe.

While this tab is open, the sample text only shows the kind chosen at the top.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Intens: Strength of the animation in percent: how much it grows, how far it moves or tilts, how bright or dark it gets. 100 is normal, 0 leaves the message still.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.MaxMessages: How many messages this area shows at once, 1 to 15. When another arrives, the oldest disappears.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Name: AutoGoblinRetainer
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Description: Adds Pinch and Sell buttons to the retainer list. Pinch visits every retainer that has listings on the Market Board and reprices each one just below the cheapest other seller, within limits you set. Sell opens a window to pick items from your bags, armoury chest and retainers and list them for you. In the settings you choose the undercut amount, the biggest cut allowed, a minimum price and the delay between searches.

Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.PinchTooltip: Reprices all your Market Board listings just below the cheapest competitor.

Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Msg.CycleDone: Pinch finished in {0} retainers: {1} repriced, {2} already the cheapest, {3} skipped.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Msg.NoSelectio: Tick some items in the window first.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Msg.NoCapacity: No retainer has a free listing slot for those items (20 per retainer).

Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Msg.SellStoppe: Listing stopped: {0} listed, {1} skipped, {2} did not fit.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Setting.PinchA: After listing, reprice every listing of the retainers it visited, new and old.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.SelectAll: Select or clear every item of this tab.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.PriceTooltip: Estimated by Universalis: the median price per unit of the sales on your world in the last 30 days. A - means there was no sale in that time. It is not the Market Board price.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Setting.MinPri: A price is never set below this, whatever the other sellers ask.
AutoGoblinRetainer takes the tedious part out of retainer sales.

Pinch: reprices every listing of your retainers just below the cheapest other seller.
Sell: opens a window where you tick items from your bags, armoury chest and retainers and list them on the Market Board.

Both buttons are next to the venture coins in the Retainer window (summoning bell). The settings are in the GoblinTweaks window (Settings button of this tweak).

While it works you will see the game's own windows open and close by themselves: it clicks exactly what you would click. Do not use the mouse on other windows until the chat says it finished. Click the button again at any time to stop it.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Help.Pinch.Tex:
Pinch visits every retainer that has something on the Market Board, opens each listing, looks at what the other sellers ask and sets the price one undercut below the cheapest one.

You can also press Pinch inside a retainer's "Sell items in your inventory on the market" list to reprice only that retainer.

- If your own listing is already the cheapest, it stays as it is.
- An HQ item only competes with HQ listings.
- If nobody else sells the item, it is left alone.
- A price is never cut by more than the limit in Settings, so a bait listing of 1 gil cannot drag your prices down.
- The Market Board refuses searches that come too quickly, so there is a short wait between items (also in Settings).
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Help.Sell.Text:
Press Sell to open the window next to the retainer list. It has a tab for your bags, your armoury chest and one for each retainer.

Tick the items you want to sell (the box in the header ticks the whole tab) and set in the Sell column how many to put up; it starts at the whole stack. Click a column title to sort by it. The Price column is only an estimate from Universalis, not the Market Board price.

Press List on Market Board. Each retainer can have 20 listings: items inside a retainer are sold by that retainer, the rest are shared between the retainers that still have room. Each item is priced just below the cheapest other seller, or at the Universalis price when nobody else sells it. With Pinch after listing ticked, all the listings of the retainers it visited are repriced afterwards.

The chocobo saddlebag has no tab: the game does not allow selling from it. Move those items to your bags first.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Help.Faq.Title: Questions
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Help.Faq.Text:
It stopped and said the game did not respond.
A window did not open in time, usually because the game was busy. Try again; what was already done is kept.

An item is missing from the list.
Only items the Market Board accepts are shown. Untradable items, collectables and items the game marks as Market Prohibited are hidden.

A retainer or the chocobo shows nothing.
The game only loads their inventory when you open them. Open each one once and it is remembered.

Some items were skipped.
The chat says which and why: the game refused them, or nobody sells them and Universalis has no price for them.

Can it sell too cheap?
Every price comes from the current Market Board. Before a big run, check the largest price cut and the lowest price in Settings.

The window or the buttons look misplaced.
The layout of the game's windows changes with your interface scale; tell the author which window and scale.
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Problem.NoPric: no price to go by (nobody sells it and Universalis has no sales)
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Problem.NotAdd: the game did not add the listing
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Problem.Unexpe: the window was not for this item
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Problem.WouldN: the game would not put it up for sale (Market Prohibited?)
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Problem.NotAll: not allowed on the Market Board (Market Prohibited)
Tweaks.AutoGoblinRetainer.Problem.Gone: it is no longer where it was
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Name: Goblin Damage Done
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Description: A damage, healing and damage-taken table of the fight in progress, for trials, raids and alliance raids: one bar per player with their job, total, per-second rate and share of the group. The table belongs to the fight, not to its phases: it stays on screen when the fight ends and is cleared when the next one starts. It counts damage and healing over time, and has an extra table (deaths and dispels) and a history of the fights of the session to look at them one by one and compare them with earlier ones. Unlock it and drag it by its title to move it.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Command.Help: Opens or closes the Goblin Damage Done settings.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Open.Help: Opens the settings window: whether the table shows, what it lists and what it counts.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Title: Goblin Damage Done
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.ResetPosition.He: Puts the table back where it starts.
Shows or hides the table on screen. Unlock it with the padlock and drag it by its title to move it.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Setting.Rows.Hel: How many players the table lists at most. If you are not among them, your own line takes the last place. An alliance raid has up to 24 players.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Setting.OverTime: Count damage and healing over time

Adds the ticks of damage and healing over time. When the game does not say whose a tick is, it is shared out among the statuses that cause it: exact when one player has one on the enemy, an estimate when several do.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Setting.Overheal: Off, healing is what was really restored (what the target was missing). On, it is the whole amount of each heal, including what was wasted on a full target.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Help.Title: Goblin Damage Done help
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Help.Overview.Te:
Goblin Damage Done shows a table of the damage, healing and damage taken of everyone in your duty, or of your party outside one, while you fight, like a damage meter, without needing any other program.

It is made for trials, raids and alliance raids: each player has a bar with their job icon, name and what they did. The bar of whoever did the most is full, and the rest are drawn in proportion to it.

The header has six buttons: the leaf switches the table between damage done, healing done and damage taken; the plus opens the extra table; the list opens the history of fights; the padlock locks or unlocks the table; the cog opens the settings and the X clears the table. Hover over them to see what each does.

To move the table, unlock it and drag it by its title. The settings open with /gdd or /goblindamagedone, with the cog, or with the Settings button in the GoblinTweaks window. While the settings are open, the table shows an example fight so you can see how each option changes it.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Help.Table.Title: Reading the table
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Help.Table.Text:
Each line reads like this:

1. Name        320.93M (1.55M, 10.3%)

First the position and the name of the player, then the total they did, and in brackets their per-second rate and their share of everything the group did.

The title says what the table shows and the name of the enemy that took the most damage, which is the boss of the fight. Damage taken is what enemies did to each player.

The color of the bar is the role of the job: blue for tanks, green for healers, red for melee, orange for physical ranged and purple for casters.

The pets and chocobos of a player count for that player.

In an alliance raid, the letter before each name is the group (A, B or C), and the settings can limit the table to your own group.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Help.Fights.Text:
The table belongs to the fight, not to the phase. A boss that changes phase, becomes untargetable for a moment or calls adds does not clear it.

A fight ends when you have been out of combat for a few seconds. The table then stays on screen with its final numbers, so you can look at it after the fight.

It is cleared when the next fight starts, whether it is against another boss or a new try at the same one. You can also clear it yourself with the X in the header of the table. The fight is not lost: it stays in the history.

Outside a duty only your own numbers are counted. Inside one, everyone in it is.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Help.OverTime.Te:
Damage and healing over time (poisons, bleeds, regeneration) is counted too.

When the game reports a tick together with the status that caused it, the tick is all of that status's owner. When it adds up the ticks of a target in one number and does not say whose each one is, it is shared out among the statuses that cause it in proportion to what each one did when it was alone on the target. The table notices which of the two the game does.

With one player's damage over time on the enemy, the numbers are exact. When several players have one on the same enemy, each one gets a part in proportion to its last tick on its own, which is an estimate: it is exact once each one has ticked alone, and until then a status weighs what the known ones do on average.

What ticks from the ground (like Salted Earth) does say whose it is, and is exact.

You can turn this off in the settings if you prefer to count only what actions do.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Help.Limits.Text:
Healing is what each heal really restored: what was wasted on a target that was already full (overheal) is left out, unless you turn it on in the settings. The health the game gives the client can be a moment late, so it is an estimate.

The table starts when someone deals damage, or heals while you are in combat. Outside a duty only you and your party are counted: players who are not in your party are left out. Fights of another zone are not mixed into the history: it starts again when a fight begins somewhere else. Only damage to enemies is counted. Damage taken is what enemies do to players with actions; damage over time on the players (poisons, bleeds) is counted as damage taken.

Deaths are counted when a player's health reaches zero. Dispels are counted from the effect the game reports when an action removes a status from someone; it has not been checked against every action, so treat it as an estimate.

A Limit Break is shown as a line of its own (Limit Break), not as damage of whoever used it. The numbers come from what the game tells your client, so they can differ a little from other programs.

If the game is updated and the function the table reads is not found, the tweak turns itself off instead of risking a crash, and says so in the GoblinTweaks window.
How opaque the backgrounds of the table are, from 0 (none) to 100. The header is drawn half as opaque as the rest.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Tooltip.Mode: Switch the table: damage done, healing done, damage taken
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Tooltip.Lock: Lock or unlock the table (it can only be dragged by its title when unlocked)
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Setting.FontSize: Size of the letters of the table, in points.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Setting.Scale.He: Makes the whole table bigger or smaller, from 50 to 200.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Setting.ShowGrou: Show the group of each player
In an alliance raid, writes the group (A, B or C) before each name.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Setting.OnlyMyGr: In an alliance raid, the table lists only the players of your own group, and the percentages are of that group. Your own group is taken as the first one the game lists; if it shows the wrong letter, tell us.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Tooltip.Extra: Open or close the extra table (critical and direct hit rates, deaths and dispels)
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Tooltip.History: Open or close the history of fights of this session
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Help.Panels.Text:
The plus opens a table with five extra numbers per player for the fight in progress, in this order, as its header says: the critical hit rate (CH%), the direct hit rate (DH%), the rate of hits that were both (CDH%), the deaths and the dispels.

By default it is docked to the right of the main table, line by line with it, so it has no names: each line is the player of the same line of the main table. The button at the top right of the extra table detaches it: it then gets the job and name of each player, lists everyone, and can be dragged by its title to wherever you like. The same button docks it back.

The rates are of the hits of the player's actions; damage over time has no such flags and is not in them. A hit that was critical and a direct hit counts in CH%, in DH% and in CDH%.

The list opens the history: every fight of this session, the last one first, with its boss, how long it lasted and the damage of the group. The bar compares their rate with the best of the session. The history keeps the last 24 fights and is emptied when the game closes. It opens where the docked extra table would, so opening one closes the other, unless the extra table is detached.

Click a fight to see its details: the same table as the main one for that fight, with the leaf still choosing between damage, healing and damage taken. If you had fought the same boss before, each player also shows how their rate changed against the last time (+12.4% or -3.0%), and the title shows the same for the whole group. Click the title of the details to go back to the list.
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Tooltip.PinOff: Detach this table: it gets the names and jobs and can be moved on its own
Tweaks.GoblinDamageDone.Tooltip.PinOn: Dock this table back next to the damage table

Tweaks.GoblinAchievements.Setting.Notify: Tell me in chat when I complete one

Tell me in chat when a tracked one is almost done
Writes a line in chat, once, when the progress of a tracked achievement reaches the percentage below.
Tweaks.GoblinAchievements.Setting.NearPe: The percentage of progress from which a tracked achievement counts as almost done.
Goblin Achievements is a browser and a tracker for the achievements of the game.

The window lists every achievement with its icon, description, category, points and state, and lets you search and filter them. Clicking one pins it to the tracker, a small table on screen that shows how far along you are with the ones you pinned.

The window opens with /gach or /goblinachievements, or with the Open achievements button in the GoblinTweaks window. The gear in the window opens the settings.
Tweaks.GoblinAchievements.Help.Loading.T:
The game does not know which achievements you have until it has asked the server, and it only does so when you open its own Achievement window. Until then, the window of this tweak cannot tell what is done and what is missing, and says so at the bottom.

The first button on the right of the top bar asks the server for it, for the achievements you have and for the almost done list. This tweak never does it on its own: it only asks when you press the button (or when you pin an achievement, for its progress).

Once the data is loaded, the window stays up to date by itself: when you complete an achievement, the game tells it.
Tweaks.GoblinAchievements.Description: A browser and a tracker for the achievements of the game. The window lists all of them with search and filters by category, state, reward and points, sorts them (even by how close you are), and has a panel with how much you have done, the achievement you selected and tools for the pinned list. The tracker, a table on screen, shows how far along you are with the ones you pinned. Chat tells you when you complete one or when a pinned one is almost done. The game only knows what you have done once it has asked the server: press the button of the window to do it, the tweak never asks on its own.

Tweaks.GoblinAchievements.Help.Browser.T:
The bar on top has the search (by name, description or category), a filter by state, the order, a filter by reward, a filter by points and a filter by category, which also says how many of each you have done.

The states are: all, missing, done, almost done (the list the game keeps for its own Near Completion page), tracked and recent (what you completed with the tweak on, with the date).

The orders include closest to done (by progress, then the almost done ones) and newest (by id).

Each line says what the achievement is, its category, its points and its state. A done line is green. Click one to see it in the panel on the right. The undo button next to the filters shows every category, state, reward and points again. The order is not a filter and stays.
Tweaks.GoblinAchievements.Help.Panel.Tex:
At the top: how many achievements and points you have done, with a bar, and what you completed in this session.

In the middle: the achievement you selected, with its description, reward, state, progress and the date you completed it, if the tweak saw it. Two buttons: Pin (or Unpin) puts it on the tracker, and Open in the game opens the game's own Achievement window on it (it waits for the window to be ready and your data loaded first).

At the bottom: the tools for the pinned list. Pin 5 closest takes the closest to done; Unpin all clears the tracker; Copy and Paste list move the ids through the clipboard; and three lists keep a set of pinned achievements that you can save and load whenever you want.
Tweaks.GoblinAchievements.Help.Tracker.T:
Select an achievement in the window and press Pin to add it to the tracker, and again to take it off. The tracker shows up to 12: each with its icon, its name and a bar with how far along you are. The bar turns gold when it gets past the percentage you set for the notices, and the number says how much you gained since you turned the tweak on, like (+5).

The progress (37 / 50) is something the game only says when asked, one achievement at a time. The tweak asks when you pin one, and again when you press the refresh button of the window; it asks one by one, a couple of seconds apart. Until the answer comes, the tracker shows a question mark.

Unlocked, the tracker is dragged from anywhere. In the settings you can lock it, hide it when it is empty, list the closest to done first, and change its opacity and font size.
Tweaks.GoblinAchievements.Help.Notices.T:
When you complete an achievement, a line in chat says which and how many points it gave, another says how many you have completed in this session, and it is taken off the tracker if it was pinned. It is also kept in the Recent list.

When the progress of a tracked achievement gets to the percentage you set (90 % by default), another line says you are almost there. It says it once per achievement.

Both can be turned off in the settings. They need the game to have loaded your achievements: before that they stay quiet.
Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Name: Goblin Loot
Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Description: A table of what each member of your party did with the items of the loot list: Need, Greed or Pass, and the number they rolled, with an arrow on the one that got the item. It has its own window, which opens next to the loot window and keeps the last rolls. The game only says who has chosen as it happens; what they chose and the numbers arrive when the roll is over.

Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Help.Overview.Title: What it does
Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Help.Overview.Text:
Goblin Loot shows, in a window of its own, what each member of your party did with each item of the loot list: Need, Greed or Pass, and the number they rolled.

The game only shows you your own number on the item. What the others rolled is in the chat, in a long line for each roll that is easy to lose. Here it is in a table.

The window opens by itself next to the loot window when an item is added to the list, and it keeps the last 8 items, so you can look at a roll after the loot window has closed.

Commands
/gloot opens or closes the window.
Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Help.Table.Title: Reading the table
Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Help.Table.Text:
On the left are the items, the newest first, each with how many players have chosen (for example 3/4) and, when the roll is over, the winning number. Press one to see it.

On the right, above the table, are the icon and the name of the item. Below it, a row for each member of your party and a column for NEED, GREED and PASS:

? in orange: the player has not chosen yet.
? in grey: the player has chosen, but the game does not say what until the roll is over.
A green number: what the player rolled, in the column they chose. The arrow marks the one that got the item.
OK in green: the player passed.
X: what the player did not choose.

Below the table it says who is still to choose, and when the roll is over, who got the item.
Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Help.Timing.Title: When you see it
Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Help.Timing.Text:
The game says who has chosen as it happens, but it does not say what they chose, and the numbers of the others are not told until the roll is over: when everyone has chosen or the time runs out. That is why the table shows question marks while the roll is open, and fills in all at once at the end.

Your own choice and your number are known at once, as in the game's window.

The game never says a Pass. Whoever chose and has no roll when it is over is shown as having passed.

Only your party is shown: in an alliance raid, the other parties are left out. If two equal items are in the list at the same time, they can be mixed up.
Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Help.Settings.Title: Settings
Tweaks.GoblinLoot.Help.Settings.Text:
Open the settings from the cog at the bottom left of the window, or from the main GoblinTweaks window.

Open when loot appears: opens the window by itself next to the loot window.

Follow the loot window: the table shows the item you select in the game's loot window.

Language: the window of this tweak can be in a different language than GoblinTweaks. The choice is at the top of the settings.

The window remembers where you leave it.
